scope: Full coverage of currently announced U.S. post-retirement commercial-reactor restarts: Crane (existing thread), Palisades and Duane Arnold. Historical U.S. TVA long-shutdown recoveries added at Browns Ferry and Sequoyah. International selection spans Japan, Canada, Armenia, Argentina, Taiwan and South Korea; it is not claimed to include every routine outage or every world restart.

pali-cost.title: Nuke plants an important source of energy, employment
pali-cost.facts: Palisades commercial operation December 31, 1971; historical construction cost $149 million.

pali-sale.title: Entergy completes sale of Palisades Power Plant to Holtec
pali-sale.facts: Palisades shut May 20, 2022; sale to Holtec completed June 28, 2022 for decommissioning.

pali-loan.title: LPO Updates • Issue 23 • October 2024
pali-loan.facts: DOE closed an up-to-$1.52 billion loan guarantee September 30, 2024; financing, not a published total restart cost.

pali-status.title: Historic First: Palisades Transitions Back to Operations Status
pali-status.facts: Palisades transitioned to operations status August 25, 2025 after July 24 licensing approvals; this did not establish an electricity-generating restart.

pali-load.title: Palisades Begins the Process for Loading Fuel in its Reactor Vessel, Embarking on a Meticulous Progression to Restart: Holtec’s Finest Hour
pali-load.facts: Fuel loading began August 30, 2026. Operator describes 805 MW electrical output and required subsequent testing and inspections.

pali-recovery.title: Holtec’s Engineering and Manufacturing Prowess Delivers Breakthrough Fuel Assembly Recovery at Palisades
pali-recovery.facts: October 21, 2026 announcement: tilted fuel assembly recovered and transferred to spent fuel pool; a restart obstacle removed, not a completed generating restart.

pali-target.title: Palisades restart delayed by fuel-handling issue
pali-target.facts: Earlier fuel-handling problem delayed restart; later October 21 Holtec recovery announcement supersedes the unresolved-obstacle status.

duane-close.title: NextEra Energy Duane Arnold, LLC; Duane Arnold Energy Center; Exemption
duane-close.facts: Licensee certified permanent cessation of power operations August 10, 2020. October 12 relates to fuel-removal certification, not the actual last generating day.

duane-ppa.title: NextEra Energy and Google Announce New Collaboration to Accelerate Nuclear Energy Deployment in the U.S.
duane-ppa.facts: October 27, 2025 announcement: 25-year Google agreement; target fully operational by first quarter 2029.

duane-loan.title: Energy Department Closes $1.9 Billion Loan to Restart Duane Arnold Nuclear Plant
duane-loan.facts: DOE release dated September 8, 2026: loan up to $1.9 billion; proposed 615 MW electrical restart, subject to NRC approval.

duane-faq.title: Duane Arnold Energy Center | FAQ
duane-faq.facts: Operator anticipates full operation by first quarter 2029, conditional on approvals.

duane-budget.title: $1.9 billion federal loan moves Duane Arnold nuclear plant closer to restart
duane-budget.facts: NextEra has not publicly disclosed total restart cost; company says multiple billions. The $1.9 billion loan is not a total capital budget.

tva-history.title: Tennessee Valley Authority — 2008 Form 10-K
tva-history.facts: Issuer annual report: five TVA units shut in 1985; Sequoyah returns May/November 1988; Browns Ferry 2 May 1991 and 3 November 1995; Unit 1 pre-commercial operation June 2, 2007.

tva-cost.title: TVA Office of Inspector General — Review of Browns Ferry Nuclear Plant Unit 1 Operating Issues Since the Restart in May 2007
tva-cost.facts: September 3, 2008 report, page 3: total project through FY2007 approximately $1.84 billion, including revenue credits and an AFUDC adjustment; $3 million budgeted FY2008 but reported year-to-date credit $2.1 million. Closing cost is not the original estimate.

browns-home.title: TVA: Browns Ferry Nuclear Plant
browns-home.facts: TVA says May 2002 board decision, Unit 1 idle since 1985, recovery completed 2007; original plant began operating 1974.

browns-cost-open.title: Browns Ferry Nuclear Power Plant
browns-cost-open.facts: All three reactors shut in 1985; Units 2/3 returned 1991/1995; Unit 1 restarted 2007 for about $1.8 billion. Issuer closing cost is more precise at $1.84 billion before AFUDC.

seq-record.title: Sequoyah Nuclear Plant Comprehensive Records Schedule
seq-record.facts: TVA original records: Unit 1 commercial July 1, 1981; Unit 2 June 1, 1982. Both shut August 1985; restart authorizations May 1988 (Unit 2), November 1988 (Unit 1).

kk-return.title: Kashiwazaki-Kariwa 6 resumes commercial operation
kk-return.facts: Unit 6 reactor startup January 21, 2026 interrupted by alarm January 22; commercial return April 16, 2026 at 16:00 Japan time. 1356 MWe gross.

kk-operator.title: (Comment) Commercial Operation of Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Station Unit 6
kk-operator.facts: TEPCO states commercial operation resumed April 16, 2026 at 16:00 local time.

kk-cost.title: Japan restarts operations at world’s largest nuclear plant, 15 years after Fukushima disaster
kk-cost.facts: Nearly 1.2 trillion yen invested in site safety upgrades since 2011; this covers the plant, not a published Unit 6-only allocation.

onagawa-index.title: OE Information related to Onagawa Unit 2 restart
onagawa-index.facts: Operator-release chronology: first reactor startup October 29, 2024; grid generation November 15; later checks and restarts; commercial return December 26, 2024.

onagawa-grid.title: Onagawa Nuclear Power Station Unit 2 connects to the grid
onagawa-grid.facts: November 15, 2024 at 18:00 Japan time: grid connection and generation; 825 MW gross.

onagawa-return.title: Onagawa Nuclear Power Station Unit 2 starts Commercial Operation
onagawa-return.facts: Commercial return December 26, 2024 at 16:00 Japan time; 825 MW gross.

onagawa-cost.title: Tohoku Electric Power — CDP disclosure
onagawa-cost.facts: Cost to realize Onagawa 2 restart opportunity 570 billion yen, including shared public safety facilities. This is the completed safety-measures scope, not all later counter-terrorism facilities.

shimane-start.title: Shimane 2 restarts after 13 years being offline
shimane-start.facts: Reactor startup December 7, 2024; 789 MWe net; offline since January 2012.

shimane-return.title: The Summary of Financial Results for FY 3/2025
shimane-return.facts: Operator confirms December 7 startup, December 23 grid connection and January 10, 2025 commercial return; different from stale database restart marker.

shimane-cost.title: Shimane 2 Highlights Progress in Japan’s Nuclear Restart Program
shimane-cost.facts: Safety-upgrade estimate revised upward to 600 billion yen. Shared station safeguards and the later anti-terrorism facility scope should not be silently combined.

bruce-history.title: History - Bruce Power
bruce-history.facts: Units 2/1 laid up in 1995/1997. Units 4/3 returned 2003/2004. 2005 agreement led to Units 1/2 refurbishment; both returned in 2012.

bruce-project.title: Nuclear Power in Canada
bruce-project.facts: Units 1/2 restart project increased to C$4.8 billion. Unit 1 grid September 2012 and commercial October; Unit 2 grid October and commercial November 2012. Combined project, no invented per-unit allocation.

bruce-complete.title: ARER2022 - Bruce Power
bruce-complete.facts: Operator retrospective confirms successful 2012 completion of Bruce A restart and return of Units 1 and 2. 2022 unit output: 6.7 and 5.9 TWh.

armenia-history.title: Nuclear Power in Armenia
armenia-history.facts: Metsamor units closed after 1988 earthquake; 1993 decision to restart Unit 2; restart in 1995 after 6.5 years. Later upgrades have different budgets from the 1995 restart.

armenia-return.title: Second Birth of the ANP
armenia-return.facts: Operator dates Unit 2 restart to November 5, 1995.

embalse-cost.title: Recent Licensing Experiences in Argentina
embalse-cost.facts: Regulator presentation: Embalse shutdown December 31, 2015; criticality January 4, 2019; total project USD 2,149 million; gross output uprated to 683 MW.

embalse-start.title: Volvió a funcionar este viernes la Central Nuclear de Embalse
embalse-start.facts: January 4, 2019 reactor startup; about USD 2.140 billion initially reported, superseded by regulator’s USD 2.149 billion total.

embalse-return.title: Embalse plant returns to service
embalse-return.facts: Ministry announced commercial return May 30, 2019, after January criticality and testing; gross electrical output 683 MW.

taiwan-history.title: Nuclear Power in Taiwan
taiwan-history.facts: Maanshan and Kuosheng feasibility endorsed November 2025; Maanshan restart application March 2026. Chinshan not feasible due to dismantled key equipment; Lungmen never commercially operated.

maanshan-close.title: Taiwan completes nuclear phase-out, leaves door open
maanshan-close.facts: Maanshan Unit 2 disconnected May 17, 2025 at end of licence, ending Taiwan generation.

maanshan-apply.title: 核三廠 - 核能安全委員會
maanshan-apply.facts: Official chronology: licence renewal/restart application received March 27, 2026; plan review completed September 24, 2026.

maanshan-review.title: 核安會完成核三廠再運轉計畫審查作業，持續執行現場查證，確認台電公司依計畫執行
maanshan-review.facts: September 24, 2026 review completion; onsite verification and later safety work continue. This is not a restart licence or operating reactor.

maanshan-target.title: Taiwan considers returning to nuclear power after decade phasing it out
maanshan-target.facts: As early as 2028 discussed for Maanshan; conditional prospect rather than a confirmed operating date.

kuosheng-close.title: Taiwanese reactor enters retirement
kuosheng-close.facts: March 14, 2023 report says Unit 2 taken offline. Database permanent-shutdown marker March 15; distinguish stopping generation from formal licence/date marker.

kuosheng-plan.title: KMT demands Lai apologize as nuclear power restart nears approval
kuosheng-plan.facts: September 3 reporting discusses Kuosheng restart planning; its assertion of a March application for both plants is not independently resolved. Regulator confirmation is needed for Kuosheng formal application status.

kori-close.title: South Korea Approves Criticality For Kori-2 As Reactor Restarts After Three-Year Shutdown
kori-close.facts: Kori 2 commercial July 25, 1983; shutdown April 8, 2023; regulator criticality permission April 2026.

kori-return.title: South Korean reactor restarts after three-year outage
kori-return.facts: KHNP says operations resumed April 4, 2026 after a 35-month improvement project. Licence extension approved November 2025 through 2033.
